text:
devon: Kicking off bring-up for a new inference cluster in us-central2 (prod-infer-uc2). Need to lock GPU capacity and file quota requests this week. Who can help with cloud quota + procurement handoff?
sara: I can take quota requests. Do we know target GPU type/count and expected QPS? need that for the request form.
devon: Target is 64 x A10G equivalent to start (8 nodes x 8 gpus). Steady-state QPS ~600 req/s, burst to 2k. Latency-sensitive, want reserved capacity + burst pool.
ajay: For quota ask we should split: per-region GPU quota, per-project vCPU + IPs, and GCE accelerators. Also request a short-term burst reservation window for initial soak.
maria: Budget note: reserved capacity + 3-month commit will save ~18% vs on-demand. Finance needs a short justification doc for the commit. I'll draft.
sara: OK, I'll file the quota request. Dev, paste the minimal payload I should send to cloud support and the procurement ticket text.
devon: Copy below — use this in support/procurement tickets:
```
Project: redwood-prod-inference
Region: us-central2
Cluster name: prod-infer-uc2
Accelerator type: A10G (or compatible)
Accelerator count: 64 (8 x 8)
Requested reservation: dedicated capacity reservation for initial 90 days; allow burst pool up to +50% for 2-4 hours/day during training/validation windows
Reason: New inference cluster launch to serve RLHF model variants; need predictable latency and capacity during rollouts
Expected peak traffic: 2000 req/s; avg 600 req/s
Contact: devon@redwood.ai, infra-oncall@redwood.ai
Cost center: INF-PLAT-03
```
sara: Perfect. I'll attach the cluster perf profile and the sample BCP (business case) from Maria.
ops-oncall: Heads-up: network egress IP allocation will need 8 static IPs for node pools + 2 NATs. Ask for a soft hold on ephemeral IP quota so the bootstrap doesn't fail. Also request a VPC peer quota if we will peer to customer VPCs.
ajay: Also include the quota for persistent disks and regional snapshots; bootstrapping 8 nodes with 1.5TB PD each needs headroom.
devon: Noted — add PD quota + snapshot schedule.
maria: I'll attach the finance justification to the procurement ticket and cc ops.
infra-bot: Reservation request created: RQ-4721 — note: provisioning window pending provider approval (expected 48-72 hrs).
sara: Filed support case #CS-19845 and procurement ticket #PUR-2219. Support returned an initial quota estimate asking for exact machine types (e.g., n2-standard-16 vs n2-standard-32).
devon: We're planning on n2-standard-32 for control plane and n2-highmem-32 for worker control services. GPU nodes: custom image on n1-highmem-8 + 8x A10G.
ajay: For faster approval, propose a two-phase reservation: 1) reserve 32 GPUs for immediate launch, 2) queue remaining 32 as pending burst reservation. Provider tends to approve smaller immediate holds quicker.
sara: I'll update CS-19845 with two-phase approach.
ops-oncall: Preflight checklist (quick):
• confirm quotas requested (accelerators, vCPU, IPs, PD, firewall rules)
• create TEMP billing commit for 90d in PUR-2219
• tag resources with team=infra, env=prod, cluster=prod-infer-uc2
• create SOC audit log export to customer-kafka for 30d
• schedule network prime window (2 hours) with netops
• set up autoscaler policy and warm nodes with a 'priming' job
sara: I'm adding the checklist to the ticket and pinging netops.
devon: One more thing — can we include a lightweight validation harness we run on first 4 GPUs? simple infer loop to validate NVLink/peer, warm KV cache, and confirm latency < 70ms p50. Example script: 
```bash
# run on new node
docker run --rm redwood/infer-smoke:latest 
  --model=redwood-base-7b 
  --warm=1000 
  --check-latency=70
```
This returns non-zero on fail.
ops-oncall: Good. We'll bake that into the bootstrap job and gate traffic with a canary route.
maria: If procurement approves, finance wants a short runbook for cancelling the commit within the first 14 days if perf doesn't match. Keep the cancellation steps documented in PUR-2219.
ajay: Also propose we request provider SLA credits for initial launch window in case of capacity issues. sometimes they agree to a partial SLA for new reservations.
sara: CS updated with two-phase reservation + SLA ask + IP/pd numbers. Waiting on provider reply.
infra-bot: Support case CS-19845 updated by sara at 1742633421.
devon: If provider pushes back, fallback plan: spin up a smaller cluster in us-west4 (usable within 6-8 hrs) and use cross-region routing for read-only traffic while we wait for full capacity in us-central2. Need to confirm cross-region latency and costs.
ajay: Cross-region fallback will add egress costs and slight RTT bump; we'll estimate cost delta and add to PUR-2219.
sara: Provider replied: can approve 32 GPUs immediate; remaining 32 in 5-7 business days pending data center stock confirmation. They asked for a signed commit to guarantee 50% utilization during the first 30 days.
maria: Finance: we can sign a 3-month commit if they lock both phases within 10 business days. I'll negotiate.
devon: Ok let's accept 32 now, queue remainder. Action items:
- sara: update CS-19845 + attach PD/vCPU/IP numbers (due EOD)
- ajay: update Terraform reservation module with dual-phase plan + tags (due tomorrow)
- maria: finalize finance justification and cancellation runbook (due EOD)
- ops-oncall: schedule network prime slot + create bootstrap job for smoke tests (due tomorrow)
- devon: prep canary routing policy and load generator for soak (due tomorrow)
sara: Done, updated support case and linked tickets.
infra-bot: Reservation partial-approved: RQ-4721-PRT (32 GPUs) at 1742634010.
ops-oncall: I'll run the bootstrap tomorrow at 03:00 UTC; will post results here.
devon: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after bootstrap. :thumbsup:
